 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE DIVYESH A. JOSHI
Date : 04/10/2024  ORAL ORDER 1. Rule. Learned APP waives service of notice of Rule for and on behalf of respondent - State.

2. The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with the FIR being C.R. No.11200051230876 of 2023 registered with the Dungra Police Station, District Valsad for the offence punishable under Sections 498A and 306 of the Indian Penal Code.
3. Heard Mr. Ramnandan Singh, learned advocate for the applicant; Mr. Niraj Sharma, learned APP for the respondent - State.

4. Mr. Ramnandan Singh, learned advocate for the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/18717/2024 ORDER DATED: 04/10/2024 undefined applicant-accused submits that this is the successive bail application, earlier application was preferred after submission of charge-sheet, which was Abdulkalam S/O Mukhtyar Abdulrasid ... vs State Of Gujarat on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38294253/
1 withdrawn with liberty to approach this Court after certain period of time.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that the present application is preferred after a period of 08 months.

He further submits that the applicant-accused is arrested on 15.05.2023 and since then, he is in judicial custody and therefore,
considering the period of incarceration spent by the applicant in judicial custody, the bail application may be entertained.
He further submits that the charge is framed and in all 22 persons have been cited as witnesses, yet not single witness examined.
He further submits that the trial would take considerable long period of time to conclude the proceedings.

Under the circumstances,
learned advocate for the applicant prays that the applicant may be enlarged on bail on any suitable terms and conditions.

5. Mr. Niraj Sharma, learned APP appearing on behalf of the respondent-State has objected the present bail application with the vehemence and submitted that specific name and role of the present applicant-accused is clearly spelt out in the body of the FIR.

He further submits that the span of marriage life of the applicant is less than 01 year and as per section-113A of the Evidence Act, the presumption of guilt can be drawn against the present applicant.

Considering the role attributed to the applicant-accused at the time of commission of crime, this is a fit case wherein discretionary power of this Court is not required to be exercised in favour of the applicant- accused.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/18717/2024 ORDER DATED: 04/10/2024 undefined 6.
The learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties do not press for further reasoned order.

7. I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers of the investigation and considered the allegations levelled against the applicant and the role played by the applicant.

This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40.
9.

sentences.text: In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against the applicant in the FIR, without discussing the evidence in detail, prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.

If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue warrant or take appropriate action in the matter.
12. Bail bond to be executed before the lower Court having NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/18717/2024 ORDER DATED: 04/10/2024 undefined jurisdiction to try the case.
